source.title: Case Study: Interpreting, Manipulating, and Controlling CLIP With Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: Tests sparse-feature recovery and use in a CLIP image encoder, extending the analysis to a real multimodal model and image-generation setting rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Reports SAE training statistics, qualitative feature findings, and qualitative results from manipulating feature groups. Values used to tune visualizations and choose clustering thresholds are setup choices, not results. The post does not report a controlled comparison of feature geometry or a systematic measurement of steering effects.
record.test_reason: Trains an SAE on a real model (CLIP ViT-g-14 pooled image embedding) and reports sparse, interpretable features and their granularity. This bears on V4 in a new, non-LLM setting and on V5's 'canonical units' claim. All evidence beyond the training statistics is qualitative.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that any image can be decomposed into concepts, which are groups of SAE features clustered by k-means. They find these concepts more interpretable and useful than single features for steering diffusion models, and suggest grouping may help SAEs in other domains.
record.recipe_differences: Trains a vanilla 64x SAE on real CLIP image embeddings and groups active feature directions with activation-weighted spherical k-means; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors say feature granularity depends on SAE sparsity, clustering thresholds depend on the SAE, and visualization settings differ by diffusion model.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation magnitude of SAE features tracks visual salience: lowering a fog feature weakens fog, and lowering a subject feature shrinks the subject.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature activation magnitude corresponds to the strength of the encoded property in generated outputs.

record.problems: The authors prioritize selected samples they intuitively consider interesting and acknowledge this may miss unexpected behavior. Interpretability judgments are not supported by a stated systematic human evaluation; steering outcomes are qualitative and lack reported controls or effect sizes. Explained variance is 65%.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported. Visualization scales, template-feature fractions, clustering thresholds, and k-selection details are described as tuning choices rather than outcomes.

untested.parts: No toy model, geometry or sparsity-dependent phase transition.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No LLMs and no neuron-level distribution of features. Only the pooled CLIP image embedding is studied.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or runs, or comparison across dictionaries.
No test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post, not peer-reviewed, and the evidence is mostly qualitative with author-selected samples. The SAE run was chosen by eyeballing feature visualizations. V4 is linked only as a new-setting (vision encoder) extension, since V4 names LLMs.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric arrangement is tested.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE feature recovery in CLIP's pooled image embedding and use with image-generation models, not feature distribution across neurons in LLMs.
Examines interpretability and usefulness of individual features versus grouped concepts, but does not measure whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs or inputs, or canonical units.
Uses linear feature directions in an SAE but does not test whether underlying model features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Trained a vanilla SAE on CLIP image embeddings using 64x expansion.
rows.note: The study reports this as the size of the learned SAE dictionary.
rows.check: 81,920 features follows directly from the chosen 64x expansion of 1280 dimensions. It is a design choice, not a result.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Measured dead and alive features in the trained SAE.
rows.note: The post states that dead features never fire.
rows.check: The dead-feature fraction (~26%) is a training diagnostic. It does not show whether sparse features exist in the model.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Measured the average number of active SAE features per image.
rows.note: The post explains this as an average of 60 active features on any image.
rows.check: Sparsity of about 60 active features out of about 60k alive. This is CLIP's pooled image embedding, not an LLM.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Measured explained variance of the SAE on the new dataset.
rows.note: The post says this is lower than the previous ImageNet run, attributing the difference probably to the greater variety and difficulty of the LAION-2B images.
rows.check: Only 65% explained variance, so the dictionary recovers the representation incompletely. No baseline is given.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Inspected SAE feature activations and their visual interpretations.
rows.value: The post reports hundreds of active features for an image, with multiple features sometimes representing the same subject or pattern; it also says features can encode distinct nuances.
rows.note: The authors say the features are not simply redundant and that individual features can express nuances; the study does not quantify these observations.
rows.check: Features look interpretable (V4). But multiple similar features encode one subject's nuances and must be grouped into concepts, so single features are not the natural unit (V5). Qualitative and author-selected samples only.

rows.subject: laion/CLIP-ViT-g-14-laion2B-s12B-b42K
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature descriptions across SAE sparsity regimes.
rows.measure: Qualitative feature granularity and reconstruction error
rows.value: The post says sparser SAEs tend to encode subjects more generically and combine fewer features for a concept, while suffering higher reconstruction error.
rows.note: No sparsity settings, numerical comparison, or controlled results are given.
rows.check: Feature granularity changes with SAE sparsity, which bears on canonicity (V5). The sparsity settings are unstated and there is no numeric comparison. It does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: Kadinsky 2.2
rows.operation_detail: Manipulated groups of active SAE features in CLIP space and diffused an image from the resulting embedding.
rows.value: The post reports that groups of features can be manipulated as units to steer generation and provide more interpretable and useful control.
rows.note: No numerical effect size or controlled comparison is reported. The post says visualization values depend on the diffusion model.
rows.check: This mainly reports the performance of the authors' own grouping and steering method, with no rate or effect size. It bears on V5 only in that the authors argue groups, not single features, are the useful unit. Removed from V4.

rows.subject: Stable Cascade
rows.operation_detail: Applied grouped-feature steering through CLIP conditioning during image generation.
rows.value: The post says steering works equally well for Stable Cascade as for the prototype model.
rows.note: No numerical effect size or controlled comparison is reported.
rows.check: Same as R7: a qualitative claim that steering also works in Stable Cascade. This is method performance and is removed from V4.

relationships.condition: CLIP ViT-g-14 pooled image embedding, vanilla 64x SAE (non-LLM setting)
relationships.reason: The SAE yields a sparse code (L0 about 60) with qualitatively interpretable features (R3, R5).
relationships.display_finding: The SAE produced a sparse code with L0 of about 60 and features that were qualitatively interpretable.

relationships.condition: Same SAE on varied LAION-2B images
relationships.reason: The dictionary explains only 65% of variance, lower than on ImageNet, so recovery is incomplete (R4).
relationships.display_finding: The dictionary explained only 65% of variance, less than on ImageNet, so recovery was incomplete.

relationships.condition: CLIP SAE features compared across sparsity levels and under grouping
relationships.reason: Feature granularity depends on SAE sparsity, and single features split a concept's nuances so that groups are the natural unit; all evidence is qualitative (R5-R8).
relationships.display_finding: Feature granularity depended on SAE sparsity, and single features split a concept's nuances so that groups were the natural unit; all evidence is qualitative.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CLIP image embeddings and the tested image-generation setting
reader_labels.reason: The trained SAE has many active sparse features, and the post reports interpretable feature activations and qualitative steering with feature groups (R1-R5, R7-R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested CLIP SAE representation and grouped-feature controls
reader_labels.reason: The post reports multiple features for similar subjects and says larger groups of features are more interpretable and useful for control, while not testing completeness or stability (R5-R8).
